title.zh: 卷461 列傳二百四十八 宋庆 吕本元 徐邦道 马玉昆 依克唐阿 荣和 长顺
title.en: Volume 461 Biographies 248: Song Qing, Lv Benyuan, Xu Bangdao, Ma Yukun, Yi Ke Tang A, Rong He, Zhang Shun
title.raw: 卷461 列傳二百四十八 宋庆 吕本元 徐邦道 马玉昆 依克唐阿 荣和 长顺

sentences.zh: 列傳二百四十八

translations.literal: Biographies 248
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 248

sentences.zh: 宋慶呂本元徐邦道馬玉昆依克唐阿榮和長順宋慶，字祝三，山東萊州人。

translations.literal: Song Qing, Lv Benyuan, Xu Bangdao, Ma Yukun, Yi Ketang'a, Rong He, and Zhang Shun. Song Qing, style Zhushan, was a native of Laizhou, Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qing, Lv Benyuan, Xu Bangdao, Ma Yukun, Yi Ketang'a, Rong He, and Zhang Shun. Song Qing, whose style was Zhushan, came from Laizhou in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 家貧落魄，聞同里宮國勳知亳州，往依為奴。

translations.literal: His family was poor and he was down on his luck; hearing that a fellow townsman, Gong Guoxun, was magistrate of Bozhou, he went to rely on him as a servant.
translations.idiomatic: Poor and adrift, he learned that a man from his home district, Gong Guoxun, had become magistrate of Bozhou and went to serve him as a household retainer.

sentences.zh: 亳捻孫之友偽就撫，慶察其意叵測，請擊之。

translations.literal: The Bozhou Nian bandit Sun Zhiyou feigned submission; Qing perceived his intentions to be unpredictable and requested to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Nian rebel Sun Zhiyou at Bozhou pretended to accept pacification, Qing sensed his motives were untrustworthy and asked permission to strike him.

sentences.zh: 國勳壯其志，署為州練長。

translations.literal: Guoxun admired his resolve and appointed him head of the prefectural militia.
translations.idiomatic: Guoxun was impressed by his spirit and made him head of the prefectural militia.

sentences.zh: 之友降，遂接統其眾，號奇勝營，薦授千總。

translations.literal: When Zhiyou surrendered, Qing then took over his forces, styled them the Qisheng Battalion, and was recommended for appointment as battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhiyou submitted, Qing took command of his troops, organized them as the Qisheng Battalion, and was recommended for the rank of battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 自是守宿州，剿豫匪，釋鳳陽圍，保徐、泗後路。

translations.literal: From then on he garrisoned Suzhou, suppressed bandits in Henan, lifted the siege of Fengyang, and secured the rear of Xuzhou and Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he held Suzhou, hunted bandits in Henan, broke the siege of Fengyang, and kept the lines to Xuzhou and Sizhou secure.

sentences.zh: 逾三歲，擢至總兵，賜號毅勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: After more than three years he was promoted to regional commander and granted the title Yiyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: Within three years he rose to regional commander and received the honorific title Yiyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 既貴，過亳，謁所主，仍易僕廝服，執事上禮益恭，人傳為美談。

translations.literal: Once he had become eminent, passing through Bozhou he called on his former master, again changed into servant's dress, and in performing his duties showed even greater respect; people spread this as a fine story.
translations.idiomatic: After he had risen high, he passed through Bozhou to visit his former master, once more put on a servant's garb, and waited on him with even greater deference—a story people loved to repeat.

sentences.zh: 同治改元，唐訓方撫安徽，裁臨淮軍，而以三營屬慶，毅軍自此始。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tongzhi reign, Tang Xunfang became governor of Anhui, disbanded the Linhuai Army, and placed three battalions under Qing; the Yijun thus began.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tongzhi reign began, Tang Xunfang took charge of Anhui, cut back the Linhuai Army, and assigned three battalions to Qing—the origin of the Yijun, or Resolute Army.

sentences.zh: 三年，苗沛霖圍蒙城，慶絕其餉道。

translations.literal: In the third year, Miao Peilin besieged Mengcheng; Qing cut off his supply routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tongzhi, Miao Peilin laid siege to Mengcheng, and Qing severed his supply lines.

sentences.zh: 會僧格林沁軍至，轟擊之，寇宵遁。

translations.literal: When Sengge Rinchen's army arrived, they bombarded the rebels, and the bandits fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Sengge Rinchen's forces then arrived and shelled the enemy until the rebels broke away under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 苗酋死，慶為安撫餘眾，自壽州正陽關所蒞皆下。

translations.literal: The Miao chieftain died; Qing pacified the remaining followers, and all places from Shouzhou to Zhengyang Pass submitted.
translations.idiomatic: After the Miao leader died, Qing pacified his remnant bands, and every post from Shouzhou to Zhengyang Pass came under his control.

sentences.zh: 兩淮告寧，調赴豫。

translations.literal: The two Huai regions reported peace, and he was transferred to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Huai basin was quiet, he was ordered to Henan.

sentences.zh: 時張曜為翼長，慶往訪，詳詢地勢寇情。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Yao was deputy commander; Qing went to call on him and inquired in detail about terrain and enemy conditions.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yao was then serving as deputy commander; Qing paid him a visit and questioned him closely about the terrain and rebel movements.

sentences.zh: 曜喜曰：「諸將無問及此者，君來，豫之福也！

translations.literal: Yao said with pleasure: "None of the other generals has asked about such matters—your coming is Henan's good fortune!"
translations.idiomatic: Yao exclaimed with delight, "No other general has troubled to ask about these things. Your arrival is a blessing for Henan!"

sentences.zh: 」遂與交驩。

translations.literal: " They thereupon became close friends.
translations.idiomatic: The two men soon became fast friends.

sentences.zh: 明年，授南陽鎮總兵。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed regional commander of Nanyang Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed regional commander of the Nanyang garrison.

sentences.zh: 無何，曹州賊勢熾，慶被困鄧州刁河店，會糧罄，勢且不敵。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits at Caozhou grew fierce; Qing was trapped at Diaohedian in Dengzhou; provisions ran out, and the situation was untenable.
translations.idiomatic: Before long rebel strength at Caozhou surged; Qing was pinned down at Diaohedian in Dengzhou, his grain exhausted and his position untenable.

sentences.zh: 乃令部將馬玉昆率壯士三百，潛出立營通饋運，軍氣復振，寇乃解去。

translations.literal: He then ordered his subordinate Ma Yukun to lead three hundred stalwarts to slip out secretly, establish a camp, and open supply lines; army morale revived, and the bandits withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his lieutenant Ma Yukun with three hundred picked men to steal out, establish a camp, and reopen the supply route; morale rallied, and the rebels drew off.

sentences.zh: 已而張總愚決河圖北犯，慶據堤迎擊，敗之，西走；

translations.literal: Soon afterward Zhang Zongyu breached the river intending to invade north; Qing held the dike and met the attack, defeated him, and he fled west.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zongyu soon breached the Yellow River in a bid to push north; Qing held the embankment, beat him back, and drove him west.

sentences.zh: 而任柱、賴文光復竄豫，湘軍將劉松山助慶軍盡驅入楚疆，豫略平。

translations.literal: But Ren Zhu and Lai Wenguang again fled into Henan; the Hunan Army general Liu Songshan aided Qing's forces in driving them entirely into Huguang territory, and Henan was largely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Zhu and Lai Wenguang then slipped back into Henan; Liu Songshan of the Hunan Army joined Qing in driving them into Huguang, and Henan was largely quiet.

sentences.zh: 巡撫李鶴年因增練兩大軍，令曜領嵩武軍，而以毅軍專屬慶。

translations.literal: Governor Li Henian accordingly enlarged the training of two great armies, placing the Songwu Army under Yao while the Yijun was assigned exclusively to Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Li Henian expanded two major forces, putting Zhang Yao in charge of the Songwu Army while the Yijun alone remained under Qing.

sentences.zh: 六年，與曜扼黃河，蹙捻至山東，聚而殲之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, together with Yao he held the Yellow River, pressed the Nian into Shandong, and annihilated them in a mass engagement.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he and Yao blocked the Yellow River, cornered the Nian in Shandong, and destroyed them in a decisive battle.

sentences.zh: 論功，賞黃馬褂，更勇號格洪額。

translations.literal: For merit he was rewarded with a yellow riding jacket and his brave title was changed to Gehong'e.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he received a yellow riding jacket and a new honorific title, Gehong'e.

sentences.zh: 時總愚南擾河津，偪解州，詔慶與曜分守河北。

translations.literal: At the time Zongyu was raiding south along the Yellow River crossings and pressing Jiezhou; an edict ordered Qing and Yao to divide the defense of the north bank of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyu was then harrying the river crossings south of the Yellow River and threatening Jiezhou; the court ordered Qing and Yao to divide the defense of the north bank.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，捻竄畿疆，慶率師入衛，轉戰雄、任、祁、高間，與諸軍大破之，總愚赴水死。

translations.literal: After a year the Nian raided the capital region; Qing led his army to guard the capital, fought between Xiong, Ren, Qi, and Gao, and with the other armies inflicted a great defeat; Zongyu drowned himself.
translations.idiomatic: A year later the Nian broke into the metropolitan district; Qing marched to the capital's defense and fought through Xiong, Ren, Qi, and Gao counties until the allied armies routed them and Zongyu drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 予二等輕車都尉，授湖南提督。

translations.literal: He was granted the second-rank title of Commandant of Light Chariots and appointed provincial military commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was ennobled as a second-class Commandant of Light Chariots and made provincial military commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 八年，左宗棠西征，慶引兵從，抵神木，再戰再捷。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when Zuo Zongtang marched west, Qing led troops in his train, reached Shenmu, and won victory after victory.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he followed Zuo Zongtang on the western campaign, reached Shenmu, and won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，命參哈、寧剿匪事，旋移督西川，皆在軍遙領。

translations.literal: The next autumn he was ordered to take part in suppressing banditry in Ha and Ning, and soon afterward was transferred to govern Sichuan—all while he remained with the army and held his posts at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn he was ordered to help suppress unrest in Ha and Ning, and soon after was transferred to the governorship of Sichuan, holding both posts remotely while still in the field.

sentences.zh: 十三年，河、狄撫回閃殿臣叛，楚軍戰失利​​。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the pacified Hui of He and Di, Shan Dianchen, rebelled, and the Chu Army suffered defeat in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Shan Dianchen, a pacified Hui leader of He and Di, rose in revolt, and the Chu Army was beaten in the field.

sentences.zh: 時慶駐涼州，奉檄往援。

translations.literal: At the time Qing was stationed at Liangzhou and received orders to go to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Qing was then at Liangzhou and marched to their relief on orders from the court.

sentences.zh: 三日馳五百餘裡，抵沙泥站，眾縛其渠以獻，誅之，事遂定。

translations.literal: In three days he rode more than five hundred li, reached Shani Station, the masses bound their leader and presented him; he was executed, and the affair was settled.
translations.idiomatic: He covered more than five hundred li in three days, reached Shani Station, where the people had already bound their chief and handed him over; Qing had him executed, and the disturbance ended.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，師還。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangxu his troops came home.

sentences.zh: 六年，徙防旅順，十餘年，軍容稱盛。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to garrison Lüshun; for more than ten years his army's bearing was acclaimed as outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was posted to Lüshun, where for more than a decade his command was regarded as the finest in the service.

sentences.zh: 醇賢親王奕枻被命巡閱，嘆為諸軍冠，親解袍服贈之。

translations.literal: Prince Chunxian Yikuang was ordered to inspect the troops, exclaimed that Qing's force was foremost among all armies, and personally removed his robe and gave it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chunxian Yikuang inspected the troops, declared Qing's unit the best in the army, and personally took off his own robe and gave it to him.

sentences.zh: 兩宮眷遇優渥，加太子少保、尚書銜。

translations.literal: The two palaces showed him exceptional favor, adding the titles Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister.
translations.idiomatic: The empresses dowager treated him with exceptional favor, raising him to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 二十年，中日失和，慶統毅軍發於旅順，與諸軍期會東邊九連城。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, when China and Japan fell out, Qing led the Yijun out from Lüshun to rendezvous with the other armies at Jiuliancheng on the eastern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Guangxu, war broke out with Japan; Qing led the Yijun from Lüshun to join the other forces at Jiuliancheng on the Manchurian border.

sentences.zh: 軍未集而平壤已失，廷旨罷總統葉志超，以慶代之。

translations.literal: Before the armies had assembled, Pyongyang was already lost; the court ordered the dismissal of supreme commander Ye Zhichao and replaced him with Qing.
translations.idiomatic: The armies had not yet gathered when Pyongyang fell; the court removed supreme commander Ye Zhichao and put Qing in his place.

sentences.zh: 慶與諸將行輩相若，驟禀節度，多不懌，以故諸軍七十餘營散無有紀。

translations.literal: Qing was of about the same generation as the other generals; suddenly placed under his command, many were displeased, and for this reason the more than seventy battalions of the various armies were scattered without discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Qing was roughly the same age as his fellow commanders, and many resented suddenly taking orders from him; more than seventy battalions therefore fought without coordination.

sentences.zh: 又坐守江北一月，以待日軍過義州，慶頓中路九連城，嚴戒備。

translations.literal: He also sat guarding the north of the river for a month, waiting for the Japanese to pass Yizhou; Qing held the central route at Jiuliancheng under strict alert.
translations.idiomatic: He also waited a month north of the Yalu for the Japanese to pass Yizhou while Qing held Jiuliancheng on the central line under tight guard.

sentences.zh: 日軍渡鴨綠江，戰失利，直趨鳳凰城，退扼大高嶺。

translations.literal: The Japanese crossed the Yalu; the battle went badly, and they pressed straight toward Fengcheng; Qing retreated to hold Dagao Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: When the Japanese crossed the Yalu the Chinese were beaten and the enemy drove toward Fengcheng; Qing fell back to hold Dagao Ridge.

sentences.zh: 旅順圍亟，朝命聶士成守之，敕慶往援。

translations.literal: The siege of Lüshun was urgent; the court ordered Nie Shicheng to defend it and commanded Qing to go to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Lüshun was in desperate straits; the court put Nie Shicheng in charge of its defense and ordered Qing to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 頓蓋平，屢搗金州不得進，而旅順已失。

translations.literal: He halted at Gaiping, repeatedly struck at Jinzhou but could not advance, and Lüshun had already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: He halted at Gaiping and repeatedly probed Jinzhou without success, while Lüshun had already been lost.

sentences.zh: 慶退守熊岳，自請治罪，被宥。

translations.literal: Qing retreated to defend Xiongyue, requested punishment for himself, and was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Qing withdrew to Xiongyue, asked to be punished, and was forgiven.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復州又失。

translations.literal: Before long Fuzhou was lost as well.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhou soon fell as well.

sentences.zh: 日軍西陷海城，慶亟赴之，擊敵感王寨。

translations.literal: The Japanese in the west captured Haicheng; Qing hastened there and attacked the enemy at Ganwangzhai.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese took Haicheng to the west; Qing hurried there and attacked them at Ganwangzhai.

sentences.zh: 前軍方勝，後隊訛傳敵拊背，駭潰，復退守田莊台，遼陽益危。

translations.literal: The vanguard had just won when the rear ranks, on a false rumor that the enemy was striking from behind, panicked and fled; they again retreated to defend Tianzhuangtai, and Liaoyang grew more perilous.
translations.idiomatic: His vanguard was winning when rumor spread in the rear that the Japanese were attacking from behind; the troops panicked and fled back to Tianzhuangtai, and Liaoyang grew more precarious.

sentences.zh: 慶凡五攻城弗能拔，朝廷思倚湘軍，命慶與吳大澂佐劉坤一軍。

translations.literal: Qing assaulted the city five times without being able to take it; the court thought to rely on the Hunan Army and ordered Qing and Wu Dacheng to assist Liu Kunyi's force.
translations.idiomatic: Qing assaulted the city five times without success; the court turned to the Hunan Army and ordered Qing and Wu Dacheng to serve under Liu Kunyi.

sentences.zh: 慶率徐邦道、馬玉昆兵萬二千人頓太平山，戰卻之，大澂敗入關。

translations.literal: Qing led Xu Bangdao and Ma Yukun with twelve thousand troops to hold Taiping Mountain, fought and repelled the enemy; Dacheng was defeated and fled inside the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Qing took twelve thousand men under Xu Bangdao and Ma Yukun to Taiping Mountain, beat the Japanese back, while Dacheng was routed and fled inside Shanhaiguan.

sentences.zh: 慶方以三萬人駐營口，聞警，還扼遼河北岸；

translations.literal: Qing was then stationed at Yingkou with thirty thousand men; hearing the alarm, he returned to hold the north bank of the Liao River.
translations.idiomatic: Qing had thirty thousand men at Yingkou; when word came of the emergency he hurried back to hold the north bank of the Liao.

sentences.zh: 而日軍盡以所獲砲列南岸猛攻，慶軍潰而西，於是遼河以東盡為日有矣。

translations.literal: But the Japanese arrayed all the captured artillery on the south bank and attacked fiercely; Qing's army broke and fled west, and thus everything east of the Liao River came under Japanese possession.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese lined the captured guns along the south bank and hammered his position; Qing's army broke and fled west, and everything east of the Liao fell to Japan.

sentences.zh: 詔褫職留任。

translations.literal: An edict stripped him of office but left him on duty.
translations.idiomatic: The court stripped him of rank but kept him in command.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，徙守山海關，入覲，釋處分。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to guard Shanhaiguan; on presenting himself at court his punishment was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was posted to Shanhaiguan; at court his punishment was lifted.

sentences.zh: 和議成，留豫軍三十營屬之，賜名武衛左軍，駐錦州。

translations.literal: When peace was concluded, thirty battalions of the Yu Army were left under him, granted the name Wuwei Left Army, and stationed at Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was made, thirty battalions of the Yu Army were left with him under the new name Wuwei Left Army, garrisoned at Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，卒，晉封三等男，予建祠，諡忠勤。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he died; posthumously ennobled as a third-class baron, granted a memorial shrine, posthumous name Zhongqin.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-eighth year, was posthumously raised to third-class baron, granted a memorial shrine, and given the posthumous name Zhongqin, Loyal and Diligent.

sentences.zh: 子天傑，五品京堂，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Tianjie, a fifth-rank official at court, inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tianjie, a fifth-rank court official, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 慶從戎久，年幾八十，短衣帕首，躞蹀冰雪中，與士卒同甘苦，人以為難雲。

translations.literal: Qing had been in the army a long time; nearing eighty, in short coat and headcloth he picked his way through ice and snow, sharing hardship with the soldiers—people regarded this as hard to achieve.
translations.idiomatic: Qing had soldiered for decades; nearing eighty he still wore a soldier's short coat and headcloth, trudging through ice and snow and sharing his men's hardships—a feat people admired as rare.

sentences.zh: 呂本元，安徽滁州人。

translations.literal: Lv Benyuan was a native of Chuzhou, Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Lv Benyuan came from Chuzhou in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 初隸李鴻章軍，隨剿粵匪、捻匪，轉戰蘇、皖、魯、豫各省。

translations.literal: At first he served under Li Hongzhang's army, followed in suppressing Guangdong bandits and Nian rebels, and fought in Jiangsu, Anhui, Shandong, and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He first served under Li Hongzhang, helped suppress the Taiping and Nian rebels, and fought across Jiangsu, Anhui, Shandong, and Henan.

sentences.zh: 援鄂、援陝屢立功，歷保總兵，賞強勇巴圖魯勇號。

translations.literal: In relief of Hubei and Shaanxi he repeatedly won merit, was repeatedly recommended for regional commander, and rewarded with the brave title Qiangyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself relieving Hubei and Shaanxi, rose to regional commander, and received the honorific title Qiangyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 鴻章總督直隸，調入直。

translations.literal: When Hongzhang became governor-general of Zhili, Benyuan was transferred into Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Hongzhang became governor-general of Zhili, Benyuan was transferred there.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，授四川重慶鎮，仍留統盛軍馬步各營。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangxu he was appointed to Chongqing Garrison in Sichuan but remained to command the cavalry and infantry battalions of the Sheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangxu he was named commander of the Chongqing garrison in Sichuan but stayed on to lead the Sheng Army's horse and foot battalions.

sentences.zh: 中日戰起，檄本元統隊出關，兼程至安州。

translations.literal: When the Sino-Japanese war broke out, an order summoned Benyuan to lead his troops beyond the Pass; he marched day and night to Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When war with Japan began he was ordered beyond the Pass and marched day and night to Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 平壤失，從宋軍退守大高嶺。

translations.literal: When Pyongyang fell, he followed Song's army in retreat to hold Dagao Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: After Pyongyang fell he withdrew with Song Qing's force to hold Dagao Ridge.

sentences.zh: 本元令各軍夜樹旗各要隘，廣設疑兵，亙二百餘裡。

translations.literal: Benyuan ordered the various armies by night to plant flags at every strategic pass, widely deploying decoy forces stretching more than two hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Benyuan had the allied units raise flags by night at every pass and spread dummy camps along more than two hundred li of front.

sentences.zh: 敵至，疑頓不前，乘其疲襲擊之，復與聶軍敗之分水嶺。

translations.literal: When the enemy arrived they hesitated and did not advance; taking advantage of their fatigue he raided them, and again with Nie's army defeated them at Fenshuiling.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese halted in uncertainty; Benyuan struck while they were weary, and with Nie Shicheng's troops later routed them at Fenshuiling.

sentences.zh: 議成，還直。

translations.literal: When negotiations were concluded, he returned to Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was made he returned to Zhili.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，拳禍起，署天津鎮，擢直隸提督，統淮、練各軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the Boxer calamity arose; he acted as commander of Tianjin Garrison, was promoted to provincial military commissioner of Zhili, and commanded the Huai and militia armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, when the Boxer rising began, he acted as commander of the Tianjin garrison, was promoted to provincial military commissioner of Zhili, and took charge of the Huai and militia forces.

sentences.zh: 剿匪受彈傷，事平，賞黃馬褂。

translations.literal: While suppressing bandits he was wounded by gunfire; when affairs were settled he was rewarded with a yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: He was shot while hunting down bandits; when order was restored he received a yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 調浙江，勤訓練，尤嚴治盜，常親督隊入山搜剿，連斃匪首。

translations.literal: Transferred to Zhejiang, he diligently trained troops and was especially strict in suppressing bandits, often personally leading detachments into the mountains to search and exterminate them, killing bandit chiefs in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Zhejiang, he drilled his troops relentlessly and cracked down hard on banditry, often leading search parties into the hills himself and killing several chiefs in succession.

sentences.zh: 浙省議裁綠營，本元贊畫始就緒。

translations.literal: Zhejiang province deliberated on cutting the Green Standard Army; Benyuan assisted in planning until the matter was brought to completion.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhejiang debated cutting the Green Standard Army, Benyuan helped plan the reform through to completion.

sentences.zh: 宣統二年，病，乞罷。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuantong he fell ill and requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xuantong he fell ill and asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 徐邦道，四川涪州人。

translations.literal: Xu Bangdao was a native of Fuzhou, Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Bangdao came from Fuzhou in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 初從楚軍討粵寇，積勳至參將。

translations.literal: At first he followed the Chu Army in campaigning against the Guangdong rebels, accumulating merit until he reached the rank of deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: He first campaigned with the Chu Army against the Taiping rebels and rose to deputy commander on merit.

sentences.zh: 還本籍籌防，解城圍，遷副將。

translations.literal: Returning to his native place to organize defense, he lifted a siege and was promoted to brigade commander.
translations.idiomatic: Back in his home district to organize defense, he raised a siege and was promoted to brigade commander.

sentences.zh: 越境援陝西漢中，賜號冠勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Crossing the border to aid Hanzhong in Shaanxi, he was granted the title Guanyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed into Shaanxi to relieve Hanzhong and received the honorific title Guanyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 旋坐漢中失守，褫職。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, on account of the loss of Hanzhong, he was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon stripped of rank when Hanzhong fell.

sentences.zh: 嗣從副將楊鼎勳援蘇，再援浙、閩，以戰功釋處分。

translations.literal: Later he followed the brigade commander Yang Dingxun in relief of Jiangsu, then again aided Zhejiang and Fujian, and through battle merit his punishment was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: He later served under brigade commander Yang Dingxun in Jiangsu, then in Zhejiang and Fujian, and won back his rank through battlefield service.

sentences.zh: 同治六年，從劉銘傳剿平東捻，复官。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tongzhi he followed Liu Mingchuan in pacifying the eastern Nian and was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tongzhi he helped Liu Mingchuan destroy the eastern Nian and was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 明年，張總愚犯減河，邦道嚴扼橋口，大敗之。

translations.literal: The next year Zhang Zongyu attacked the Jian River; Bangdao strictly held the bridgehead and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Zhang Zongyu struck at the Jian River; Bangdao held the bridgehead firmly and routed him.

sentences.zh: 更勇號鏗僧額，遷總兵，署江蘇徐州鎮。

translations.literal: His brave title was changed to Kengseng'e; he was promoted to regional commander and acted as commander of Xuzhou Garrison in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: His honorific title was changed to Kengseng'e, he was made regional commander, and acted as commander of the Xuzhou garrison in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 光緒四年，擢提督，調駐天津軍糧城，授正定鎮。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Guangxu he was promoted to provincial military commissioner, transferred to garrison Junliangcheng at Tianjin, and appointed to Zhengding Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Guangxu he became provincial military commissioner, was posted to Junliangcheng near Tianjin, and given command of the Zhengding garrison.

sentences.zh: 東事起，慶以旅順守將赴防九連城，李鴻章別令薑桂題等守旅順，邦道助之。

translations.literal: When the eastern affair arose, Qing as Lüshun garrison commander went to defend Jiuliancheng; Li Hongzhang separately ordered Jiang Guiti and others to defend Lüshun, and Bangdao assisted them.
translations.idiomatic: When war in the east began, Qing left his post at Lüshun for Jiuliancheng; Li Hongzhang put Jiang Guiti and others in charge of Lüshun, with Bangdao to assist.

sentences.zh: 日軍入貔子窩，邦道語諸將曰：「金州若失，則旅順不可守，請分兵御之。

translations.literal: When the Japanese entered Biziwowo, Bangdao said to the generals: "If Jinzhou is lost, Lüshun cannot be held—please divide forces to defend it."
translations.idiomatic: When the Japanese landed at Biziwowo, Bangdao told the other commanders, "If we lose Jinzhou, Lüshun cannot be held. Send detachments to block them."

sentences.zh: 」諸將各不相統，莫之應。

translations.literal: " The generals were not under unified command and none responded.
translations.idiomatic: No one answered, for the commanders answered to no common authority.

sentences.zh: 邦道自率所部趨大連灣。

translations.literal: Bangdao himself led his own unit toward Dalian Bay.
translations.idiomatic: Bangdao marched his own troops toward Dalian Bay.

sentences.zh: 是時銘軍分統趙懷益守其地，邦道至，固請兵，乃分步旅隨邦道行。

translations.literal: At the time Zhao Huaiyi of the Ming Army's detached command was defending that place; when Bangdao arrived he urgently requested troops, and infantry detachments were then divided to follow Bangdao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Huaiyi of the Ming Army held the bay; Bangdao pressed him hard for reinforcements, and Zhao finally sent infantry to march with him.

sentences.zh: 日軍大集，遂佔金州，進偪大連，懷益奔旅順。

translations.literal: The Japanese gathered in force, then occupied Jinzhou and pressed toward Dalian; Huaiyi fled to Lüshun.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese concentrated in strength, took Jinzhou, and pushed on Dalian; Huaiyi fled to Lüshun.

sentences.zh: 越十日，日軍來爭旅順，諸將相顧無措，邦道率殘卒至，憤甚，思自效，請增兵，不許；

translations.literal: After ten days the Japanese came to contest Lüshun; the generals looked at one another at a loss; Bangdao arrived with his remnant troops, was deeply angered, wished to devote himself, requested reinforcements, and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later the Japanese moved on Lüshun; the commanders were helpless until Bangdao arrived with his battered remnant, furious and eager to redeem himself; he asked for reinforcements and was refused.

sentences.zh: 請械，許之，乃率眾拒戰土城子，挫之。

translations.literal: He requested arms and was permitted; he then led the masses to resist at Tuchengzi and repulsed them.
translations.idiomatic: He was given arms, led his men to fight at Tuchengzi, and beat the Japanese back.

sentences.zh: 日軍大至，乃退。

translations.literal: When the Japanese arrived in great force, he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When overwhelming Japanese forces arrived, he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 道員龔照嶼先一日遁，諸將亦奪民船以濟，蓋日軍未至而旅順已墟矣。

translations.literal: The circuit intendant Gong Zhaoyu had fled the day before; the generals also seized civilian boats to cross—the Japanese had not yet arrived and Lüshun was already a ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit intendant Gong Zhaoyu had fled the day before; the generals seized civilian boats to escape—Lüshun was already abandoned before the Japanese arrived.

sentences.zh: 邦道奔復州依慶，詔褫職。

translations.literal: Bangdao fled to Fuzhou and relied on Qing; an edict stripped him of office.
translations.idiomatic: Bangdao fled to Fuzhou and joined Qing; the court stripped him of rank.

sentences.zh: 慶令守蓋州，邦道自牛莊移師還，而蓋平亦已失，合章高元擊之，弗勝。

translations.literal: Qing ordered him to defend Gaizhou; Bangdao moved his army back from Niuzhuang, but Gaiping had already fallen; together with Zhang Gaoyuan he attacked but could not win.
translations.idiomatic: Qing ordered him to hold Gaizhou; Bangdao marched back from Niuzhuang, but Gaiping had already fallen; he and Zhang Gaoyuan attacked together without success.

sentences.zh: 桂題往援，邦道請夜搗蓋平，桂題辭，諸軍皆退營口。

translations.literal: Guiti went to the rescue; Bangdao requested a night assault on Gaiping; Guiti declined, and all the armies retreated to Yingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Guiti came to relieve them; Bangdao proposed a night raid on Gaiping, but Guiti refused and the whole force fell back to Yingkou.

sentences.zh: 邦道乃從慶擊敵太平山，與玉昆力戰卻之，俄仍敗潰。

translations.literal: Bangdao then followed Qing in attacking the enemy at Taiping Mountain; with Yukun he fought fiercely and repelled them, but soon they were again defeated and routed.
translations.idiomatic: Bangdao then fought with Qing at Taiping Mountain; he and Ma Yukun drove the Japanese back, but were soon routed again.

sentences.zh: 復與湘軍將李光久攻海城，亦弗克，遂退。

translations.literal: Again with the Hunan Army general Li Guangjiu he attacked Haicheng but likewise could not take it, and then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Hunan Army general Li Guangjiu in another assault on Haicheng, failed again, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，卒，复官，予優恤。

translations.literal: After a year he died; his office was restored and favorable condolence was granted.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he died; his rank was restored and generous posthumous honors were granted.

sentences.zh: 馬玉昆，字景山，安徽蒙城人。

translations.literal: Ma Yukun, style Jingshan, was a native of Mengcheng, Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yukun, whose style was Jingshan, came from Mengcheng in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 以武童從宋慶攻捻，積功至都司，賜號振勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: As a military cadet he followed Song Qing in attacking the Nian, accumulated merit until he reached the rank of commander, and was granted the title Zhenyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: As a military cadet he campaigned with Song Qing against the Nian, rose to the rank of commander, and received the honorific title Zhenyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 任柱等困慶登州，玉昆銳身馳救，圍立解，繇是以驍果名。

translations.literal: When Ren Zhu and others besieged Qing at Dengzhou, Yukun dashed to the rescue with keen resolve; the siege was immediately lifted, and from this he gained a reputation for valor.
translations.idiomatic: When Ren Zhu besieged Qing at Dengzhou, Yukun charged to the rescue and lifted the siege at once, earning a name for fierce courage.

sentences.zh: 捻平，擢總兵。

translations.literal: When the Nian were pacified, he was promoted to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: After the Nian were suppressed he was made regional commander.

sentences.zh: 剿秦、隴回，數獲勝，更勇號曰博奇。

translations.literal: In suppressing the Hui of Qin and Long he won many victories; his brave title was changed to Boqi.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting the Hui rebels in Shaanxi and Gansu he won repeated victories and received a new honorific title, Boqi.

sentences.zh: 既克肅州，賜頭品服。

translations.literal: After Suzhou was taken, he was granted first-rank court dress.
translations.idiomatic: After the capture of Suzhou he was granted first-rank court dress.

sentences.zh: 嗣從金順出嘉峪關，連下烏魯木齊、昌吉、瑪納斯，擒其渠黑瞎子。

translations.literal: Later he followed Jin Shun out through Jiayu Pass, successively took Urumqi, Changji, and Manas, and captured their chieftain Heixiazi.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Jin Shun beyond Jiayu Pass, took Urumqi, Changji, and Manas in succession, and captured the rebel chief known as Black Blind One.

sentences.zh: 天山南北告寧，賞黃馬褂，予世職。

translations.literal: North and south of the Tianshan reported peace; he was rewarded with a yellow riding jacket and granted a hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: When the lands north and south of the Tianshan were quiet, he received a yellow riding jacket and a hereditary commission.

sentences.zh: 玉昆居西域先後十餘年，收復名城以十數，暇輒使部下屯墾闢地利。

translations.literal: Yukun dwelt in the western regions for more than ten years in all, recovered more than a dozen famous cities, and in leisure moments often had his subordinates garrison and reclaim land to open up local resources.
translations.idiomatic: Yukun spent more than ten years in the far west, recovered a dozen major cities, and in quieter times had his men farm garrison lands to develop the region.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章疏薦將才，謂可繼宋慶。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang memorialized recommending him as a military talent, saying he could succeed Song Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang recommended him to the throne as a commander who could succeed Song Qing.

sentences.zh: 光緒間，調赴直隸。

translations.literal: During the Guangxu reign he was transferred to Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: During Guangxu he was transferred to Zhili.

sentences.zh: 二十年，補授山西太原鎮。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was appointed in full to Taiyuan Garrison in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was appointed commander of the Taiyuan garrison in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 會日朝構釁，玉昆統毅軍赴援，次平壤，壁南門外大同江。

translations.literal: When Japan and Korea came into conflict, Yukun led the Yijun to aid them, halted at Pyongyang, and encamped south of the city gate on the Datong River.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out between Japan and Korea, Yukun led the Yijun to the front, reached Pyongyang, and encamped south of the city on the Datong River.

sentences.zh: 日軍來攻，玉昆守東岸，血戰久，援至，敵敗去。

translations.literal: When the Japanese came to attack, Yukun defended the east bank, fought a bloody battle for a long time, reinforcements arrived, and the enemy was defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the Japanese attacked, Yukun held the east bank in a long bloody fight until reinforcements arrived and the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 已而玄武門失，葉志超令其速撤軍，乃歸平壤。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the Xuanwu Gate was lost; Ye Zhichao ordered him to withdraw his army quickly, and he returned to Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xuanwu Gate fell, Ye Zhichao ordered a rapid withdrawal, and he fell back to Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 日軍佔蓋平，諸將皆退營口。

translations.literal: The Japanese occupied Gaiping; all the generals retreated to Yingkou.
translations.idiomatic: After the Japanese took Gaiping, the commanders fell back to Yingkou.

sentences.zh: 玉昆從慶頓太平山，日軍猛攻之，玉昆戰最力，擊退其眾。

translations.literal: Yukun followed Qing in holding Taiping Mountain; the Japanese attacked fiercely; Yukun fought with greatest effort and repelled their forces.
translations.idiomatic: Yukun joined Qing at Taiping Mountain; when the Japanese attacked fiercely he fought hardest of all and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 無何，日軍大集，慶陷重圍，墜馬負創，玉昆抉圍入，翼之出，傷亡殊多。

translations.literal: Before long the Japanese gathered in force; Qing was caught in a heavy encirclement, fell from his horse and was wounded; Yukun broke through the encirclement to enter, shielded him out, and casualties were very heavy.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese soon massed in strength; Qing was surrounded, thrown from his horse, and wounded; Yukun broke through the ring, shielded him out, and losses were severe.

sentences.zh: 轉戰田莊台、感王寨，以千餘人抗強敵，屹然自全。

translations.literal: He fought at Tianzhuangtai and Ganwangzhai, with a little more than a thousand men resisted a strong enemy, and stood firm preserving himself intact.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Tianzhuangtai and Ganwangzhai, held off a superior force with barely a thousand men, and brought his command through intact.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，擢浙江提督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was promoted to provincial military commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was made provincial military commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 明年，調還直隸。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred back to Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred back to Zhili.

sentences.zh: 適拳匪肇亂，聯軍入寇，玉昆統武衛左軍御之。

translations.literal: Just then the Boxer bandits arose in disorder and the allied armies invaded; Yukun commanded the Wuwei Left Army to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Boxers rose and the allied armies invaded; Yukun led the Wuwei Left Army against them.

sentences.zh: 初戰天津，繼戰北倉，相持月餘，卒以無援退。

translations.literal: At first he fought at Tianjin, then at Beicang, held the line for more than a month, and finally withdrew for lack of support.
translations.idiomatic: He fought first at Tianjin, then at Beicang, held the line for more than a month, and finally withdrew for lack of support.

sentences.zh: 車駕西幸，命隨扈。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage went west on tour, he was ordered to accompany as escort.
translations.idiomatic: When the court fled west he was ordered to escort the emperor.

sentences.zh: 又明年，還京，加太子少保。

translations.literal: The year after that he returned to the capital and was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he returned to Beijing and was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，朝陽土寇竊發，玉昆倍道應赴，破其卡，生擒首惡鄧萊峰誅之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year local bandits in Chaoyang rose in secret; Yukun marched by forced stages to respond, broke their stockade, captured alive the chief culprit Deng Laifeng and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year bandits rose in Chaoyang; Yukun marched at forced pace, stormed their stockade, captured the ringleader Deng Laifeng alive, and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，病卒，贈太子太保，予二等輕車都尉，諡忠武。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he died of illness; posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted second-class Commandant of Light Chariots, posthumous name Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness in the thirty-fourth year, was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and second-class Commandant of Light Chariots, and given the posthumous name Zhongwu, Loyal and Martial.

sentences.zh: 依克唐阿，字堯山，扎拉里氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人，吉林駐防。

translations.literal: Yi Ketang'a, style Yaoshan, of the Zhalari clan, a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner, garrisoned at Jilin.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Ketang'a, whose style was Yaoshan, of the Zhalari clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner garrisoned at Jilin.

sentences.zh: 以馬甲從征江南。

translations.literal: As an armored cavalryman he followed the campaign in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He first campaigned in Jiangnan as a cavalryman.

sentences.zh: 移師討捻，敗張洛行於大回村、濉溪口，屢著戰績，積勳至佐領。

translations.literal: The army was shifted to suppress the Nian; he defeated Zhang Luoxing at Dahui Village and Suixi Ford, repeatedly distinguished himself in battle, and accumulated merit until he reached the rank of assistant commander.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to fight the Nian, he defeated Zhang Luoxing at Dahui Village and Suixi Ford, won repeated distinction, and rose to assistant commander.

sentences.zh: 同治初，馬賊陷伊通，依克唐阿以少襲眾，斬其酋劉果發等，又破之昌圖，攻克劉家店，复長春廳，遷協領，賜號法什尚阿巴圖魯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongzhi, mounted bandits took Yitong; Yi Ketang'a with few attacked many, beheaded their chiefs Liu Guofa and others, again defeated them at Changtu, stormed Liujiadian, recovered Changchun Subprefecture, was transferred to deputy commander, and granted the title Fashishang'a Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongzhi mounted bandits seized Yitong; Yi Ketang'a attacked with inferior numbers, killed their chiefs including Liu Guofa, routed them at Changtu, took Liujiadian, recovered Changchun, was promoted to deputy commander, and received the title Fashishang'a Batulu.

sentences.zh: 搜捕殘匪，獲白凌阿、焦西平，晉副都統。

translations.literal: In searching out remnant bandits he captured Bai Ling'a and Jiao Xiping and was promoted to vice commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Hunting down remnant bandits he captured Bai Ling'a and Jiao Xiping and was made vice commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十一年，補官黑龍江。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he received appointment in Heilongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was appointed in Heilongjiang.

sentences.zh: 光緒五年，移呼蘭，呼蘭設副都統自此始。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Guangxu he was transferred to Hulan; the establishment of a vice commander-in-chief at Hulan began from this time.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Guangxu he was posted to Hulan, where a vice commander-in-chief was established for the first time.

sentences.zh: 明年，母憂歸。

translations.literal: The next year, on his mother's death, he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he went home to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 時俄人以議改伊犁條約有違言，烏里雅蘇台參贊喜昌夙諗依克唐阿諳戰術，請敕就近募獵戶守琿春。

translations.literal: At the time the Russians raised objections to revising the Ili Treaty; the Uliastai consultant Xichang had long known Yi Ketang'a to be skilled in tactics and requested an edict to recruit hunters nearby to defend Hunchun.
translations.idiomatic: Russia was then disputing revisions to the Ili Treaty; Xichang, the consultant at Uliastai, who knew Yi Ketang'a's tactical skill, asked the court to let him recruit local hunters to defend Hunchun.

sentences.zh: 會吉林戒嚴，依克唐阿遂募兵五千擇隘分守，而自率師駐其地。

translations.literal: When Jilin was placed on alert, Yi Ketang'a then recruited five thousand troops, chose passes to divide the defense, and himself led the army to garrison the place.
translations.idiomatic: When Jilin went on alert he raised five thousand men, posted them at key passes, and led the main force in person.

sentences.zh: 琿春故重鎮，其東南海參崴，俄尤數窺伺，廷議設副都統鎮之，於是又改調琿春。

translations.literal: Hunchun was an important town of old; to its southeast was Haishenwai, which the Russians especially often watched covetously; the court deliberated on establishing a vice commander-in-chief to guard it, and he was then transferred again to Hunchun.
translations.idiomatic: Hunchun was a strategic town facing Vladivostok to the southeast, which Russia watched closely; the court decided to station a vice commander there and transferred him to Hunchun.

sentences.zh: 十年，被命佐吉林軍事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was ordered to assist in Jilin military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was ordered to assist with military affairs in Jilin.

sentences.zh: 十五年，擢黑龍江將軍。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was promoted to general of Heilongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was made general of Heilongjiang.

sentences.zh: 二十年，日朝戰起，依克唐阿請率軍自效，乃進咸鏡道，繞赴漢城迎擊，上嘉之。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year war broke out between Japan and Korea; Yi Ketang'a requested to lead troops to offer his service, advanced along the Xianjing route, and made a detour toward Seoul to meet and strike the enemy; the emperor commended him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year war broke out between Japan and Korea; Yi Ketang'a volunteered for the front, advanced along the Xianjing route, and swung toward Seoul to intercept the enemy—the emperor praised his zeal.

sentences.zh: 左寶貴軍失利平壤，日軍西進，命移駐九連城。

translations.literal: Zuo Baogui's army was defeated at Pyongyang; the Japanese advanced west; he was ordered to move his garrison to Jiuliancheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Zuo Baogui was beaten at Pyongyang and the Japanese pushed west, he was ordered to Jiuliancheng.

sentences.zh: 尋以日軍渡江來攻，復令徙上游御之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, because the Japanese crossed the river to attack, he was again ordered to move upstream to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Japanese crossed the river to attack, he was ordered upstream to block them.

sentences.zh: 依克唐阿與戰於蒲石河，連克蒲石河口、古樓子。

translations.literal: Yi Ketang'a fought them at Pushi River and in succession took Pushi River mouth and Gulouzi.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Ketang'a fought at the Pushi River and took the river mouth and Gulouzi in succession.

sentences.zh: 宋慶退駐大高嶺，依克唐阿孤軍不能獨守，遂退寬甸。

translations.literal: Song Qing retreated to hold Dagao Ridge; Yi Ketang'a's isolated army could not hold alone and therefore withdrew to Kuandian.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qing fell back to Dagao Ridge; Yi Ketang'a, isolated, could not hold alone and withdrew to Kuandian.

sentences.zh: 宋軍南援旅、大，聶士成軍接防，乃定夾攻之約。

translations.literal: Song's army went south to aid Lüshun and Dalian; Nie Shicheng's army took over the defense, and they then fixed an agreement for a pincer attack.
translations.idiomatic: Song's force went south to relieve Lüshun and Dalian while Nie Shicheng took over the line; the commanders agreed on a joint attack.

sentences.zh: 依軍由寬甸繞進賽馬集迎擊日軍，先戰懸羊砬子，連勝之草嶺河、通遠堡、草河口。

translations.literal: Yi's army made a detour from Kuandian toward Saimaji to meet and strike the Japanese, first fought at Xuanyanglazi, and in succession won at Caoling River, Tongyuan Fort, and Caohekou.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's army swung from Kuandian toward Saimaji to intercept the Japanese, fought first at Xuanyanglazi, then won at Caoling River, Tongyuan Fort, and Caohekou.

sentences.zh: 日軍大集，橫斷聶、依兩軍，士成亟趨分水嶺拊其背，依軍還擊之，陣斬一中尉。

translations.literal: The Japanese gathered in force and cut across between Nie's and Yi's armies; Shicheng hastened to Fenshuiling to strike their rear; Yi's army turned and struck them, killing a lieutenant in the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese massed and cut between Nie and Yi; Nie hurried to Fenshuiling to hit their rear while Yi counterattacked and killed a Japanese lieutenant in the field.

sentences.zh: 又西而東，大戰於金家河，軍稍挫。

translations.literal: Again from west to east, a great battle was fought at Jinjia River, and the army was somewhat checked.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting west and then east, they met the Japanese in a major battle at Jinjia River and were slightly beaten.

sentences.zh: 日軍先已佔鳳凰城，依克唐阿謀襲之，分左右翼以進，戰一面山，敵來爭，左翼潰，右翼統領永山遇伏死，依克唐阿保餘軍退，詔革職圖後效。

translations.literal: The Japanese had already occupied Fengcheng; Yi Ketang'a planned to raid it, advanced with left and right wings, fought at Yimianshan; the enemy came to contest; the left wing collapsed; the right-wing commander Yongshan met an ambush and died; Yi Ketang'a preserved the remnant army and withdrew; an edict stripped him of office to seek later merit.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese already held Fengcheng; Yi Ketang'a tried to retake it with a two-wing advance at Yimianshan; the left wing broke, right-wing commander Yongshan was ambushed and killed, and Yi Ketang'a withdrew with the survivors; the court stripped his rank pending future service.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，海城陷，遼西危棘，詔責長順守遼陽，依克唐阿助之，發帑金五十萬濟依軍。

translations.literal: After a year Haicheng fell; western Liaodong was in peril; an edict charged Zhang Shun with defending Liaoyang and Yi Ketang'a to assist him, and disbursed five hundred thousand taels from the treasury to supply Yi's army.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Haicheng fell and western Liaodong was in peril; the court ordered Zhang Shun to hold Liaoyang with Yi Ketang'a's help and sent five hundred thousand taels to supply Yi's army.

sentences.zh: 既至，議以攻為守。

translations.literal: Once they arrived, they deliberated on using attack as defense.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival they agreed that the best defense was to attack.

sentences.zh: 乃集諸將置酒，取刀刺臂血，攪而飲之，相矢以死。

translations.literal: They then gathered the generals for wine, took knives to prick their arms for blood, stirred it and drank, and pledged one another to death.
translations.idiomatic: They gathered the generals for a feast, pricked their arms and mixed the blood into their wine, and swore to fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 依軍遂進取海城，軍騰鰲堡、耿莊，數戰弗勝。

translations.literal: Yi's army then advanced to take Haicheng, encamped at Teng'ao Fort and Gengzhuang, and fought several times without victory.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's army advanced on Haicheng and camped at Teng'ao Fort and Gengzhuang, but several assaults failed.

sentences.zh: 會榮和至軍，亟趣之出。

translations.literal: When Rong He arrived at the army, they urgently urged him to go out.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong He joined the army they pressed him to take the field at once.

sentences.zh: 榮和先進北路，奪三卡，其左樹木幽深，令隱兵備抄襲，而自列陣曠野，伏槍以待。

translations.literal: Rong He first advanced on the northern route and seized three stockades; on his left the trees were deep and dense, and he ordered hidden troops to prepare for flanking raids, while he himself drew up his formation on open ground with ambush guns waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Rong He advanced on the northern route and took three stockades; on his left, in dense woods, he hid men for a flank attack while he drew up in the open with musketeers in ambush.

sentences.zh: 日軍據山巔轟擊我師，彈落積雪中，漬不發。

translations.literal: The Japanese held the mountain crest and bombarded our army; shells fell in the piled snow and, soaked through, failed to explode.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese shelled from the hilltops; their rounds landed in deep snow and failed to explode.

sentences.zh: 我師還擊，僕者眾，再發再僕。

translations.literal: Our army struck back; many gunners fell, and again they fired and again fell.
translations.idiomatic: The Chinese returned fire, but many gunners fell, fired again, and fell again.

sentences.zh: 眾爭傍山出，伏槍具舉，死以百數。

translations.literal: The masses rushed out along the mountain; the ambush guns all fired, and deaths numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese rushed along the hillside; the ambushers fired together and killed hundreds.

sentences.zh: 榮和所部募自塞邊外，善避擊，傷者恆少，所謂「東山獵戶」也。

translations.literal: Rong He's unit was recruited from beyond the frontier passes; they were skilled at evading strikes, and the wounded were always few—the so-called "Eastern Mountain hunters."
translations.idiomatic: Rong He's men were frontier hunters, skilled at dodging fire and taking few casualties—the famous "Eastern Mountain hunters."

sentences.zh: 是役以千人抗日軍數千，故依軍聲譽遠出諸軍上。

translations.literal: In this battle a thousand men resisted several thousand Japanese troops, and therefore Yi's army's reputation far exceeded the other forces.
translations.idiomatic: In this fight a thousand men held off several thousand Japanese, and Yi's army gained a reputation above all the rest.

sentences.zh: 罷戰詔下，日人將歸我遼東，依克唐阿力請三路分兵鎮懾，稱旨。

translations.literal: When the cease-fire edict was issued and the Japanese were to return Liaodong to us, Yi Ketang'a strongly requested dividing troops in three routes to garrison and overawe; this accorded with the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: When the cease-fire was proclaimed and Japan was to return Liaodong, Yi Ketang'a urged posting troops on three routes to secure the territory—the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 又條上練兵隊、築砲台、造鐵路、制槍械、開礦產、治團練六事，朝旨以礦政尤要，敕妥籌開採。

translations.literal: He also submitted in detail six items: training companies, building batteries, constructing railways, manufacturing firearms, opening mines, and organizing militia; the court's decree held mining policy especially important and ordered proper planning for extraction.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed six reforms—training units, building forts, laying railways, manufacturing arms, opening mines, and organizing militia; the court singled out mining as especially urgent and ordered careful development.

sentences.zh: 又明年，晉頭品秩，授鑲黃旗漢軍都統。

translations.literal: The next year he was advanced to first-rank standing and appointed commander-in-chief of the Bordered Yellow Banner Chinese Army.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was raised to first rank and made commander-in-chief of the Bordered Yellow Banner Chinese Army.

sentences.zh: 其秋，出為盛京將軍。

translations.literal: That autumn he went out as general of Shengjing.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he became general of Shengjing.

sentences.zh: 既蒞事，糾貪墨，整營製，晰分釐稅，歲增餉銀數十萬。

translations.literal: Once he took up affairs, he corrected corruption, put camp regulations in order, clearly divided lijin taxes, and each year increased military pay by several hundred thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: In office he punished corruption, tightened camp discipline, clarified transit taxes, and increased annual military revenue by hundreds of thousands of taels.

sentences.zh: 复撤還金州奉軍，杜俄人藉口，境內稱治。

translations.literal: He also withdrew the Fengtian troops from Jinzhou, cutting off a Russian pretext, and within the territory good order was acclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: He also pulled the Fengtian garrison out of Jinzhou, denying Russia a pretext for interference, and the region was said to be well governed.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，卒，諡誠勇，予建祠。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he died; posthumous name Chengyong, granted a memorial shrine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-fifth year, was given the posthumous name Chengyong, Sincere and Brave, and granted a memorial shrine.

sentences.zh: 依克唐阿勇而有謀，性仁厚，不嗜殺，每有俘獲，不妄戮一人。

translations.literal: Yi Ketang'a was brave and resourceful, by nature kind and generous, not fond of killing; whenever he took captives he did not recklessly execute a single person.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Ketang'a was brave and shrewd, kindly by nature, and reluctant to kill; he never executed captives without cause.

sentences.zh: 轉戰吳、皖、魯、豫，先後救出難民以十數万計，至今人屍祝之。

translations.literal: Fighting in Wu, Wan, Lu, and Yu, he successively rescued refugees numbering in the hundreds of thousands; to this day people offer sacrifices and pray to him.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning in Jiangsu, Anhui, Shandong, and Henan, he rescued refugees by the hundreds of thousands, and people still offer him sacrifices in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 初與長順訂兄弟交，長順兄事之。

translations.literal: At first he and Zhang Shun made a pact of brotherhood; Zhang Shun treated him as an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: He and Zhang Shun had sworn brotherhood, and Zhang Shun treated him as an elder brother.

sentences.zh: 及議遼陽戰守，語不協。

translations.literal: When they deliberated on defending or attacking at Liaoyang, their words did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: When they debated how to defend Liaoyang, they could not agree.

sentences.zh: 依克唐阿毅然獨任其難，曰：「孰使我為兄也者？

translations.literal: Yi Ketang'a resolutely undertook the difficulty alone, saying: "Who made me the elder brother?"
translations.idiomatic: Yi Ketang'a took on the hard part alone, saying, "Who told me to play the elder brother?"

sentences.zh: 」其雅量如此。

translations.literal: " Such was his magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 榮和，字育堂。

translations.literal: Rong He, style Yutang.
translations.idiomatic: Rong He, whose style was Yutang.

sentences.zh: 二等侍衛，官至副都統。

translations.literal: Second-rank bodyguard, rose in office to vice commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: A second-rank imperial guardsman, he rose to vice commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 戰後所部育字營多驕縱，命李秉衡查辦，革職治罪。

translations.literal: After the war his subordinate Yuzi Battalion was often arrogant and unruly; Li Bingheng was ordered to investigate, and he was stripped of office and punished.
translations.idiomatic: After the war his Yuzi Battalion grew unruly; Li Bingheng was ordered to investigate, and Rong He was stripped of rank and punished.

sentences.zh: 長順，字鶴汀，達呼裡郭貝爾氏，隸滿洲正白旗，世居布特哈。

translations.literal: Zhang Shun, style Heting, of the Daur Gorbier clan, attached to the Manchu Plain White Banner, dwelt for generations at Buteha.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shun, whose style was Heting, of the Daur Gorbier clan, belonged to the Plain White Banner and came from a family long settled at Buteha.

sentences.zh: 起家藍翎侍衛，隨文宗車駕狩熱河。

translations.literal: He began his career as a blue-plume bodyguard and followed Emperor Wenzong's carriage on the hunt at Rehe.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a blue-plume guardsman and accompanied Emperor Wenzong on the hunt at Rehe.

sentences.zh: 會馬賊陷朝陽，從大學士文祥討平之。

translations.literal: When mounted bandits took Chaoyang, he followed Grand Secretary Wenxiang in suppressing and pacifying them.
translations.idiomatic: When mounted bandits seized Chaoyang, he followed Grand Secretary Wenxiang and helped put them down.

sentences.zh: 嗣復從侍郎勝保徵捻，轉戰直、魯、皖、豫，以驍勇稱。

translations.literal: Later he again followed Vice Minister Sengbao in campaigning against the Nian, fought in Zhili, Shandong, Anhui, and Henan, and was known for fierce valor.
translations.idiomatic: He later served under Vice Minister Sengbao against the Nian, fought across Zhili, Shandong, Anhui, and Henan, and won a name for fierce courage.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，解潁州圍，以功遷二等。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he lifted the siege of Yingzhou and for merit was transferred to second rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he raised the siege of Yingzhou and was promoted to second rank for his service.

sentences.zh: 多隆阿主陝西軍事，調赴軍，至潼關，大敗寇眾，賜號恩特赫恩巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Duolong'a directed military affairs in Shaanxi; Shun was transferred to the army, reached Tongguan, inflicted a great defeat on the bandit masses, and was granted the title Entehe'en Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: When Duolong'a took charge in Shaanxi, Shun joined his command, routed the rebels at Tongguan, and received the title Entehe'en Batulu.

sentences.zh: 進攻咸陽馬家堡，被巨創，援至，又大破之，咸陽复，晉頭等。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Majia Fort at Xianyang, he received a grave wound; reinforcements arrived, and he again inflicted a great defeat; Xianyang was recovered and he was promoted to first rank.
translations.idiomatic: Attacking Majia Fort at Xianyang he was badly wounded, but when reinforcements came he routed the enemy, recovered Xianyang, and was promoted to first rank.

sentences.zh: 三年，悍回馬化隆據寧夏，分其黨駐清水堡成犄角，師久攻不下。

translations.literal: In the third year the fierce Hui Ma Hualong held Ningxia, divided his followers to garrison Qingshui Fort in a pincer position, and the army for a long time could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the rebel Ma Hualong held Ningxia and posted detachments at Qingshui Fort in support; the siege dragged on without success.

sentences.zh: 長順曰：「不先翦其羽翼，城未可克也！

translations.literal: Zhang Shun said: "If we do not first cut off his wings, the city cannot be taken!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shun said, "Unless we cut off his outposts first, we will never take the city!"

sentences.zh: 」乃自靈州襲清水堡，乘勝取寧夏，拔之，晉副都統，賜頭品服。

translations.literal: " He then from Lingzhou raided Qingshui Fort, took advantage of victory to seize Ningxia, stormed it, was promoted to vice commander-in-chief, and granted first-rank court dress.
translations.idiomatic: He struck from Lingzhou, stormed Qingshui Fort, swept on to take Ningxia, was made vice commander-in-chief, and received first-rank court dress.

sentences.zh: 時長順年未四十，而戰常陷堅。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Shun was not yet forty, yet in battle he often charged into the thick of the fight.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shun was not yet forty, yet he always led from the front.

sentences.zh: 每當兵潰時，或抄襲其後，或橫阻其前，俾潰者得整列，以是常轉敗為勝。

translations.literal: Whenever the army broke, he either raided from behind or blocked across their front, enabling the routed to re-form their ranks; by this he often turned defeat into victory.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever his men broke, he would hit the enemy from the rear or block them in front so the fugitives could reform—thus he often turned defeat into victory.

sentences.zh: 其旗幟尚白，寇望見之，輙呼曰：「小長將軍至矣！

translations.literal: His banners favored white; when bandits saw them they would cry out: "Little General Zhang has come!"
translations.idiomatic: His banners were white; at sight of them the rebels would cry, "Little General Zhang is here!"

sentences.zh: 」相與戒勿犯，其為寇所憚若此。

translations.literal: " They would warn one another not to offend him; such was the dread in which the bandits held him.
translations.idiomatic: They warned one another not to engage him—so greatly did the rebels fear him.

sentences.zh: 六年，移師蘭州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the army was shifted to Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year his command was transferred to Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時省城戎備寡，回眾數千突來犯，長順率百人隱小溝，出不意疾擊之，寇愕走，又敗之平番、皋蘭、狄道，既复規取河州，連破太子寺、高家集，被賞賚。

translations.literal: At the time the provincial capital's military preparations were few; several thousand Hui suddenly came to attack; Zhang Shun led a hundred men hidden in a small ditch, struck them unexpectedly with speed, and the bandits fled in astonishment; he again defeated them at Pingfan, Gaolan, and Didao; having recovered, he planned to take Hezhou, successively broke Taizisi and Gaojiaji, and was rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Lanzhou was lightly defended when several thousand Hui attacked; Zhang Shun hid a hundred men in a ditch and struck by surprise, routing them; he beat them again at Pingfan, Gaolan, and Didao, then took Taizisi and Gaojiaji in a drive on Hezhou and received imperial rewards.

sentences.zh: 八年，授鑲紅旗漢軍副都統。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed vice commander-in-chief of the Bordered Red Banner Chinese Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was made vice commander-in-chief of the Bordered Red Banner Chinese Army.

sentences.zh: 越二年，出署烏里雅蘇台將軍，坐事免。

translations.literal: After two years he went out to act as general of Uliastai and was dismissed on account of an affair.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he acted as general of Uliastai but was dismissed after an incident.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，复官，左宗棠調赴甘肅，歷署巴里坤領隊大臣、哈密幫辦大臣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu his office was restored; Zuo Zongtang transferred him to Gansu, and he successively acted as commanding officer at Barkol and assistant commissioner at Hami.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangxu he was restored to office; Zuo Zongtang sent him to Gansu, where he served as commanding officer at Barkol and assistant commissioner at Hami.

sentences.zh: 初，新疆南路勘界議起，當事者與俄使相持久不決。

translations.literal: At first, when the boundary survey of southern Xinjiang arose, the responsible officials and the Russian envoy faced each other in a prolonged stalemate without resolution.
translations.idiomatic: When the southern Xinjiang boundary dispute began, Chinese officials and the Russian envoy deadlocked for months.

sentences.zh: 至是，長順陟巉岩，披蒙茸，獲見高宗御書界碑，俄使始無異辭，乃定。

translations.literal: At this point Zhang Shun climbed steep cliffs, pushed through thick grass, obtained sight of the boundary stele inscribed by Emperor Gaozong, and only then did the Russian envoy cease objections and the matter was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shun then climbed the cliffs, pushed through the brush, and found the boundary stele inscribed by Emperor Qianlong; the Russians ceased to object and the line was fixed.

sentences.zh: 明年，假歸，歷授正白旗漢軍都統、內大臣。

translations.literal: The next year, on leave to return home, he was successively appointed commander-in-chief of the Plain White Banner Chinese Army and inner minister.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, on leave, he was appointed commander-in-chief of the Plain White Banner Chinese Army and inner minister.

sentences.zh: 十四年，出為吉林將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he went out as general of Jilin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he became general of Jilin.

sentences.zh: 既蒞事，賑菑荒，維圜法，均釐榷，澄吏治，清盜源，整旗務，境內一切皆治辦。

translations.literal: Once he took up affairs, he relieved famine and disaster, maintained the legal code, equalized lijin levies, clarified official administration, eliminated the sources of banditry, put banner affairs in order, and within the territory everything was brought to good governance.
translations.idiomatic: In office he relieved famine, upheld the law, equalized transit taxes, cleaned up the bureaucracy, uprooted banditry, reorganized the banners, and brought the whole province under order.

sentences.zh: 又創修吉林通志，書成上之。

translations.literal: He also newly compiled the General Gazetteer of Jilin; when the book was completed he presented it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled a new General Gazetteer of Jilin and presented it to the throne when it was finished.

sentences.zh: 二十年，日軍陷海城，遼陽危。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year the Japanese took Haicheng and Liaoyang was in peril.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year the Japanese captured Haicheng and Liaoyang was in danger.

sentences.zh: 朝命長順往援，節制奉天各軍，並嚴詔：「遼陽有失，唯長順是問。

translations.literal: The court ordered Zhang Shun to go to the rescue, placed him in command of the various armies of Fengtian, and issued a stern edict: "If Liaoyang is lost, only Zhang Shun will be held to account."
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Zhang Shun to relieve Liaoyang with command over the Fengtian armies and a stern warning: "If Liaoyang falls, Zhang Shun alone will answer for it."

sentences.zh: 」時潰軍紛集遼城下，署知州徐慶璋方閉城不令入，軍大閧。

translations.literal: " At the time routed troops gathered in confusion below Liaoyang city; the acting prefect Xu Qingzhang had just closed the gates and would not let them enter, and the army made a great uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Routed troops were massing outside Liaoyang while Acting Prefect Xu Qingzhang kept the gates shut; the soldiers rioted.

sentences.zh: 會長順領百騎至，斬閧者一，餘令還駐沙河。

translations.literal: When Zhang Shun arrived leading a hundred cavalry, he beheaded one of the rioters and ordered the rest to return and encamp at Shahe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shun arrived with a hundred horsemen, executed one ringleader, and sent the rest back to camp at Shahe.

sentences.zh: 先是長順被命以軍五千分隊應赴，先至者令壁本溪湖，自輕騎入遼陽。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhang Shun had been ordered to respond with five thousand troops in divided columns; those arriving first were ordered to encamp at Benxihu, while he himself entered Liaoyang with light cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He had been ordered to bring five thousand men in columns; the first detachments were posted at Benxihu while he rode into Liaoyang with a light escort.

sentences.zh: 亂既定，日軍諜者亦不知其止百騎也，第歸言某將軍至。

translations.literal: Once the disorder was settled, Japanese spies also did not know he had only a hundred cavalry; they merely returned saying a certain general had arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Once order was restored, Japanese spies never learned he had only a hundred horsemen and reported merely that a general had arrived.

sentences.zh: 日軍遂止弗前，遼陽乃保。

translations.literal: The Japanese then halted and did not advance, and Liaoyang was thus preserved.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese halted their advance, and Liaoyang was saved.

sentences.zh: 已而進攻海城，戰數日弗勝，長順奏趣宋慶會師，詔不許。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he advanced to attack Haicheng; after several days of fighting he could not win; Zhang Shun memorialized urging Song Qing to join forces; the edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He then attacked Haicheng without success for days; Zhang Shun asked the court to bring Song Qing to join him, but was refused.

sentences.zh: 湘軍將陳湜至，又請劉坤一令合攻，亦未果。

translations.literal: When the Hunan Army general Chen Ni arrived, he again requested Liu Kunyi to order a joint attack, but this too did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: When Hunan Army general Chen Ni arrived he again asked Liu Kunyi for a combined assault, again without success.

sentences.zh: 及日軍繞道復攻遼陽，適慶璋守靦峒峪，長順與依克唐阿回援，得無恙。

translations.literal: When the Japanese made a detour to attack Liaoyang again, Qingzhang happened to be defending Miantongyu; Zhang Shun and Yi Ketang'a returned to the rescue, and it remained unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Japanese swung around to strike Liaoyang again, Xu Qingzhang was holding Miantongyu; Zhang Shun and Yi Ketang'a hurried back and the city escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 和議成，請疾歸。

translations.literal: When peace was concluded, he requested leave to return home on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was made he asked to retire on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，復起吉林將軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was again appointed general of Jilin.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was recalled as general of Jilin.

sentences.zh: 拳亂作，俄羅斯內犯，奉天、黑龍江皆主戰，長順獨持不可。

translations.literal: When the Boxer disorder arose and Russia invaded from within, Fengtian and Heilongjiang all advocated war; Zhang Shun alone held that it should not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxers rose and Russia invaded, Fengtian and Heilongjiang urged war, but Zhang Shun alone opposed it.

sentences.zh: 又上言拳匪不可恃，東省鐵路隨地皆駐俄兵，宜善為羈縻，寧嚴守以待戰，毋先戰以啟釁。

translations.literal: He also submitted that the Boxer bandits could not be relied on, that along the eastern provinces' railway Russian troops were stationed everywhere, that they should be well managed with restraint, that it was better to hold strictly and await battle than to fight first and open hostilities.
translations.idiomatic: He warned that the Boxers were unreliable, that Russian troops were posted all along the eastern railways, and that the province should hold firm and avoid provoking a war.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其老成持重，奉、吉軍事悉屬之。

translations.literal: The emperor commended his seasoned steadiness, and all military affairs of Fengtian and Jilin were placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his seasoned judgment and placed all military affairs of Fengtian and Jilin under him.

sentences.zh: 戰釁既開，奉、黑皆罹災，而吉林安堵，人服其先見。

translations.literal: Once hostilities were opened, Fengtian and Heilongjiang both suffered disaster, but Jilin remained tranquil, and people admired his foresight.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out Fengtian and Heilongjiang were devastated while Jilin stayed calm, and people credited his foresight.

sentences.zh: 日俄之戰，守中立，獨無所犯。

translations.literal: In the Russo-Japanese War he maintained neutrality and alone suffered no violation.
translations.idiomatic: During the Russo-Japanese War he kept Jilin neutral and untouched.

sentences.zh: 三十年，卒，贈太子少保，予一等輕車都尉，諡忠靖，入祀賢良祠。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he died; posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted first-class Commandant of Light Chariots, posthumous name Zhongjing, entered for worship at the Shrine of Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirtieth year, was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and first-class Commandant of Light Chariots, given the posthumous name Zhongjing, Loyal and Tranquil, and enshrined in the Temple of Worthies.

sentences.zh: 長順聳幹赬面，鬚眉灑然。

translations.literal: Zhang Shun was tall in stature with a ruddy face; his beard and brows were free and easy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shun was tall and ruddy, with a flowing beard and brows.

sentences.zh: 富膽略，恆持短矛單騎穿賊陣，為士卒先。

translations.literal: Rich in courage and strategy, he constantly held a short spear and on a single horse pierced through the bandit formations, going before the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and resourceful, he often charged the enemy lines alone on horseback with a short spear at the head of his men.

sentences.zh: 往往以少制眾，以奇制勝，兼謀勇，一時稱良將雲。

translations.literal: He often used few to control many, used surprise to win victory, combined strategy and valor, and for a time was acclaimed as a fine general.
translations.idiomatic: He often beat larger forces with smaller ones, won by surprise, and combined shrewdness with courage; his contemporaries hailed him as a fine general.

sentences.zh: 論曰：中日之戰，淮軍既覆，湘軍隨之，唯豫軍強起支搘。

translations.literal: The commentary says: In the Sino-Japanese War, after the Huai Army was destroyed, the Hunan Army followed suit; only the Yu Army forcefully rose to prop up the situation.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: In the Sino-Japanese War the Huai Army was ruined and the Hunan Army followed; only the Yu Army rallied to hold the line.

sentences.zh: 慶與玉昆先後失利，亦不復能自振焉。

translations.literal: Qing and Yukun suffered defeats one after another and likewise could no longer revive themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qing and Ma Yukun were beaten in turn and never recovered their standing.

sentences.zh: 東三省練軍自成軍後，終未當大敵，而依克唐阿、長順一奮其氣，遂保遼陽而無失，中外稱之。

translations.literal: The trained armies of the three eastern provinces, from the time they were formed as armies, in the end never faced a great enemy; yet Yi Ketang'a and Zhang Shun, rousing their spirit once, then preserved Liaoyang without loss, and were praised within and without.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial armies of the northeast had never faced a major foe, yet Yi Ketang'a and Zhang Shun, rallying their troops once, held Liaoyang intact and won praise at home and abroad.

sentences.zh: 喪師辱國者數矣，此固差強人意者哉。

translations.literal: There have been many who lost armies and shamed the state; this is indeed somewhat stronger than what one might wish.
translations.idiomatic: The empire had suffered many humiliating defeats; this at least was a performance not altogether disappointing.
